mainTopic: רבי שמעון's limit of the five חטאות מתות to an individual's offering, explained by ריש לקיש and רבי נתן; then a new משנה on how קדשים and תמורה are each stricter than the other.
overview: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון can learn that the five חטאות מתות apply only to an individual, when some of those cases can never happen with a community. It answers that he received all five cases as one single tradition. ריש לקיש explains that four cases were taught at סיני and the people applied the rule to all five out of doubt. He proves the four were about an individual, so the unclear cases follow the clear ones. רבי נתן says only one case was taught and the people applied it to all five. The גמרא asks why they did not at least check which group that case belonged to, and answers that they forgot two things. רבי נתן then concludes the same way: the rule applies to an individual and not to a community. A new משנה begins, listing ways קדשים are stricter than a תמורה and ways a תמורה is stricter than קדשים. That list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can we learn a possible case from an impossible one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון: how can he limit the cases that could happen with a community to individuals only, by comparing them to cases that can never happen with a community?
steps.simpleTranslation: But can we learn something that is possible from something that is impossible?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי שמעון's view that the rule of חטאות מתות applies only to an individual and not to a community. He reaches that by comparing to cases that cannot happen with a community at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is that you learn a case from a case that is like it. Some of the five cases, like the owner dying, can never happen to a צבור. So how can they teach that the other cases, which can happen with a צבור, are also limited to an individual?

keyTerms.meaning: We derive / we learn one case from another
Possible: a case that can happen here
Impossible: a case that can never happen here

phrases.english: But can one derive the possible
phrases.notes: Possible means cases that really can happen with a community's offering.

phrases.english: from the impossible?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's derivation from the earlier part of the sugya.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's limiting of the five חטאות מתות to an individual's offering, learned from cases impossible for a community.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cases that are impossible for a community cannot teach a limitation (individual only) on cases that are possible for a community.

steps.title: רבי שמעון received all five cases as one tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not learn one case from another. He received all the cases together as one single הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון learns them all in one place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי שמעון is not comparing cases; all five were taught as one package.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem of learning possible from impossible only exists if you are comparing one case to another. If all five cases were handed down as one unit, the rule covers every case in the package equally. Then it does not matter that some cases cannot happen with a community.

keyTerms.meaning: In one place: as one single unit or tradition
Learned, received as a tradition

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, in one place
phrases.notes: He means all five cases were taught together as one law, not learned one from the other.

phrases.english: learns them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּחַד מָקוֹם גְּמִיר לְהוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the source: one combined tradition, not a comparison between cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון learns the communal cases from the individual cases by comparing them.
steps.terutzMaskana: All five cases came as one הלכה, so the rule applies to every case in it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון holds the five חטאות מתות are one single tradition. That is why the possible/impossible problem does not bother him.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: four cases were taught, and the people applied it to five
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that at סיני four cases of sin offerings that die were taught. Since they did not know which fifth case was different, they applied the rule to all five.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Four were given to them, and they established them as five.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains how the tradition of the five חטאות מתות came about. Only four were really given; the fifth was added out of doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original tradition had four sin offerings that die and one that is left to graze until it gets a blemish. The people forgot which one was the grazing one. So to be safe, they treated all five as sin offerings that die.

keyTerms.meaning: Were given to them, meaning taught at סיני
They established them, they set the practice

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
Four were given to them,
phrases.notes: Four kinds of sin offering that are left to die were taught; the fifth was meant to graze until it got a blemish.

phrases.english: and they established them as five.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אַרְבָּעָה נִתְּנוּ לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a further explanation of the 'one tradition' idea from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four חטאות מתות were taught at סיני, and out of doubt all five were treated as left to die.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the people made up a new law. They knew four cases die and one does not, but forgot which one, so they were strict on all five.

steps.title: The four taught cases must have been about an individual
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש proves the four taught cases were about an individual, since not all four can happen with a community. So the unclear cases are learned from the clear ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think it was about a community, do all these exist with a community? Rather, you must say: learn the unclear from the clear.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש shows which group the four taught cases belong to. They cannot be communal, because some of them never happen with a community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four cases were taught together, so they all belong to one group, either individual or צבור. Some of them cannot happen with a צבור, so the tradition must have been about an individual. The cases that were not spelled out are then learned from the ones that were spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind, you might think
Community, communal offering
Against your will, you are forced to say
Learn the unspecified from the specified

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that it was about a community —
do these exist with a community?
phrases.notes: Not all four cases can happen with a community's offering, so the four must have been taught about an individual.

phrases.english: Rather, you are forced to say —
let the unspecified be learned from the specified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's explanation by proving which group the four taught cases belong to.
steps.raayaObject: That the four taught cases were about an individual's sin offering.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic that not all four cases can happen with a community.
steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, the four cases taught at סיני were about an individual. The cases not spelled out are learned from the ones that were.

steps.title: רבי נתן: only one case was taught, and the people applied it to five
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says only one sin offering that dies was taught at סיני. Since they did not know which one, they applied the rule to all five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: One was given to them, and they established it as five.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן gives a different version of the history. Only one case was really a sin offering that dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נתן it is the opposite of ריש לקיש: one dies and four graze. Since they forgot which one dies, they were strict and treated all five as left to die.

keyTerms.meaning: One case only

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
One was given to them,
and they established it as five.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: אַחַת נִתְּנָה לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different account from ריש לקיש's in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one חטאת מתה was taught at סיני, and out of doubt all five were treated as left to die.

steps.title: Why not check whether that one case was individual or communal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי נתן: even if they forgot the exact case, they should have checked whether it was in the individual group or the communal group.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them see in which group they learned it, whether in an individual or in a community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי נתן's account. If they at least knew the group, they could have limited the rule to that group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three cases happen only with an individual, and two can also happen with a community. If they knew which group the one case came from, they would only need to be strict on that group. The other group could keep its normal rule of grazing until it gets a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them see, let them check
Order, category, group
An individual, an individual's offering

phrases.english: But let them see in which group
phrases.notes: The group means the cases that only happen with an individual versus the cases that can also happen with a community.

phrases.english: they learned it,
whether with an individual or with a community?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי נתן's statement in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נתן's claim that the doubt spread the rule to all five cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Knowing the group would limit the doubt to that group, so there is no reason to be strict on all five.

steps.title: They forgot two things
steps.stepSummary: The answer to the question on רבי נתן is that two things were forgotten, so they could not narrow it down.
steps.simpleTranslation: They forgot two things, and it was hard for them to decide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6. They could not check whether the case belonged to the individual group or the communal group, because they had forgotten that too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed they still remembered whether the one taught case was about a יחיד or a ציבור. The answer says no: they forgot both which case it was and which group it belonged to. With two unknowns, they had no way to narrow it down, so they applied the rule to all five.

keyTerms.meaning: Something forgotten
It was difficult for them; they could not resolve it

phrases.english: They forgot two things,
phrases.notes: They forgot which case it was, and also whether it was about a יחיד or a ציבור.

phrases.english: and it was difficult for them.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification: more was forgotten than the question assumed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They only forgot which specific case it was, so they could have checked the group
steps.terutzMaskana: They also forgot the group, so there was no way to narrow it down

steps.title: These cases cannot all happen with a community
steps.stepSummary: The text shows the cases cannot be about a ציבור, because they do not all apply to a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think it is about a community, can these cases even happen with a community?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי נתן's statement, which continues with the same proof as ריש לקיש: these cases must be about an individual, because they could not all happen with a community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the proof given for ריש לקיש in step 4. Some of these cases only make sense for one owner, not for a whole community. So the starting point has to be the יחיד.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind; if you would think
The community; offerings brought on behalf of all of Israel
They exist; they can happen

phrases.english: And if you would think it is about a community,
can these cases even happen with a community?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי נתן's statement from step 5, after the challenge and answer in steps 6-7. He uses the same proof ריש לקיש used in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the cases of חטאות המתות are about a יחיד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that these cases cannot all happen with a ציבור

steps.title: The unclear cases are learned from the clear ones
steps.stepSummary: The cases that are not spelled out follow the ones that are: they apply only to an individual, not to a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: So learn from this: the unspecified cases are learned from the specified ones. Just as the specified cases are about an individual and not a community, the unspecified cases are also about an individual and not a community.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן finishes his statement with the conclusion: the rule that a חטאת is left to die applies only to an individual's offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cases that are clearly about a יחיד set the pattern. The unclear cases follow that pattern, so a ציבור offering is never left to die under these rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; conclude from it
Unspecified; not spelled out
Specified; spelled out clearly
An individual; a private offering

steps.whatToRemember: The five חטאות המתות apply only to an individual's offering, never to a community's offering.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
the unspecified is learned from the specified —
just as the specified is about an individual and not a community,
so too the unspecified is about an individual and not a community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in step 8
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rule of חטאות המתות applies only to a יחיד and not to a ציבור

steps.title: The new משנה: each side has its own stringency
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens by saying that קדשים are stricter in some ways, and תמורה is stricter in other ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sacrificial animals are stricter than a substitute in some ways, and a substitute is stricter than sacrificial animals in other ways.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a general heading. It is setting up two lists that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשים are animals consecrated directly. A תמורה is an animal that became holy because someone swapped it for a holy animal. The משנה will show that neither one is simply stricter: each is stricter in different areas.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
Stringency; a way something is stricter
Animals consecrated directly as offerings
A substitute animal that became holy by being swapped for a holy one

phrases.english: MISHNA: There is stringency with sacrificial animals more than with a substitute,
and stringency with a substitute more than with sacrificial animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins; it does not depend on the earlier discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשים and תמורה are each stricter than the other in different ways

steps.title: Ways sacrificial animals are stricter
steps.stepSummary: קדשים can create a תמורה, but a תמורה cannot. A ציבור and partners can consecrate but cannot substitute. Fetuses and limbs can be consecrated but cannot be substituted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sacrificial animals are stricter because they can create a substitute, but a substitute cannot create another substitute. The community and partners can consecrate animals but cannot make a substitute. A person can consecrate fetuses and limbs, but cannot make a substitute with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three ways that regular קדשים are stronger than a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, if you swap an ordinary animal for a holy one, it becomes a תמורה. But if you swap an animal for a תמורה, nothing happens. Second, הקדש works for a ציבור and for partners, but תמורה does not. Third, you can consecrate an unborn animal or a single limb, but you cannot use them to make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Create a substitute; make a swapped animal holy
Partners who own an animal together
They consecrate; make holy
They substitute; swap an ordinary animal for a holy one
Fetuses; unborn animals
Limbs of an animal

phrases.english: Stringency with sacrificial animals more than with a substitute —
that sacrificial animals create a substitute,
but a substitute does not create a substitute.
The community and partners can consecrate,
but they cannot substitute.
And one can consecrate fetuses and limbs,
but one cannot substitute with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹמֶר בְּקָדָשִׁים מִבַּתְּמוּרָה שֶׁהַקֳּדָשִׁים עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the details of the first half of the heading in step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשים create a תמורה; הקדש works for a ציבור, partners, fetuses and limbs, while תמורה does not

steps.title: Ways a substitute is stricter
steps.stepSummary: A תמורה is stricter because its holiness takes hold even on an animal with a permanent blemish, and that animal does not go out to ordinary status.
steps.simpleTranslation: A substitute is stricter than sacrificial animals because the holiness takes hold even on an animal with a permanent blemish, and it does not go out to ordinary status.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins the second list, showing how a תמורה is stronger than regular קדשים. The list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, consecrating a permanently blemished animal only gives it monetary holiness. But if you swap a blemished animal for a holy one, the swap makes the animal itself holy. That animal also cannot simply return to ordinary status.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח
Holiness takes hold
Ordinary, non-holy status

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a blemished animal cannot become holy at all. Even when directly consecrated it gets some holiness. The point here is that through תמורה, the holiness takes hold more strongly.

phrases.english: Stringency with a substitute more than with sacrificial animals,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהַקְּדוּשָּׁה חָלָה עַל בַּעֲלַת מוּם קָבוּעַ,
phrases.english: that the holiness takes hold on an animal with a permanent blemish,
and it does not go out to ordinary status

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹמֶר בַּתְּמוּרָה מִבַּקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁהַקְּדוּשָּׁה חָלָה עַל בַּעֲלַת מוּם קָבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the details of the second half of the heading in step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through תמורה, holiness takes hold even on a permanently blemished animal, and it does not go out to חולין
